script.text: A million satellites running A.I. in orbit. U.S. regulators said yes, with a catch.

This week, the U.S. regulator FCC gave SpaceX conditional approval for up to one million Starmind satellites. They are meant to be data centers for artificial intelligence. Chair Brendan Carr calls it a bold new frontier for computing.

The catch: SpaceX asked for orbits up to two thousand kilometers. It got about one thousand, and nothing above six hundred until it files a final debris plan. The first satellite must work by twenty thirty-three, all one million by twenty forty.

About eleven thousand Starlink satellites orbit Earth now, per astronomer Jonathan McDowell. Monash University's Michael Brown says Starmind would multiply active satellites more than fifty times. The FCC rejected petitions to block it, including one from the American Astronomical Society.
Will SpaceX fly Starmind satellites in twenty twenty-seven, as it plans? Yes or no?

upload.title: FCC Clears SpaceX for 1 Million AI Satellites #shorts
upload.description:
On November 25, 2026, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission gave SpaceX conditional approval to deploy up to one million Starmind satellites meant to work as orbital data centers for artificial intelligence. The FCC allowed altitudes of about 500 to 1,002 km instead of the 2,000 km SpaceX requested, with nothing above 600 km until SpaceX files a final orbital-debris plan; the first satellite must be operating by 2033 and the full constellation by 2040. Astronomers, including Monash University's Michael Brown, warn about the impact on the night sky; the FCC rejected petitions to deny, including one from the American Astronomical Society. SpaceX says it plans to begin flying Starmind satellites in 2027.

Sources: FCC (Space Bureau order), CNN, CNBC, TechCrunch, Space.com, Spaceflight Now, GeekWire, SiliconANGLE, Gizmodo, Engadget, Advanced Television, Jonathan McDowell (satellite count).
